## What I found

`src/orders/billing.js` is already a separate, dependency-free module: 24 lines, three pure functions, **zero imports**. Editing a tax rate today touches that one file and nothing else. So the change-isolation problem the request names is largely already solved, and moving the directory changes nothing structural — all four complexity deltas are zero.

Two decisions follow. Move the file to `src/billing/` and ship import rules with it (the record calls this **BUILD-minimal**) — cheap, reversible, and it makes the boundary enforced rather than conventional. Do **not** make it a deployed service (the record calls this **DROP**): none of a service's prerequisites hold — one `package.json`, one deployable, no data store, no second team — and a network boundary cannot reduce change coupling that is already zero.

Separately, reading the code turned up the thing that actually threatens weekly billing changes: **there are no tests at all**, and there are two live defects in the billing path.

## Why it matters

`npm test` runs `node --test` against zero test files and exits green. Money arithmetic that you say changes every week has no automated check at any stage — defects in it are catchable at Stage 6 (unit test) and are currently only catchable at Stage 10 (production), a rank distance of 5 and the largest gap in the repo. Meanwhile `reprice()` updates `order.total` but never regenerates `order.invoice`, so after a reprice the stored invoice carries the old pre-tax figure; and `invoiceFor()` emits line amounts that sum to gross while its `total` is the discounted amount, so lines never reconcile to total whenever a discount applies. Both ship today.

If you do the directory move and nothing else, you get an enforced boundary and keep both bugs and the zero-coverage gap.
